scene: one adult in plain clothes stands whole-figure, side view, beside one huge plain wooden crate with a lid whose top rises far above the adult's head and whose width is more than twice the shoulders. The adult looks small beside it and the wall behind is plain.
must: a crate towering far above the person's head.
avoid: a crate the size of a shoe (klein); a tall thin shape (hoog); a long low box (lang); a heavy crate with a person bending under it (zwaar).
contrast: Pair with klein. The only difference is the crate: far above the person's head here, no higher than the person's shoe there.
example_nl: Ons nieuwe huis is erg groot.
example_en: Our new house is very big.
alt: Een man staat naast een enorme kist die veel hoger is dan zijn hoofd.

scene: one adult in plain clothes stands whole-figure, side view, beside one tiny plain wooden crate with a lid that is no higher than the adult's shoe and no wider than a hand. The adult looks like a giant beside it and the wall behind is plain.
must: a crate no higher than the person's shoe.
avoid: a huge crate beside the person (groot); a short person on tiptoe (klein, the person sense); a thin line or sliver (dun); a crate far away drawn small by distance (ver).
contrast: Pair with groot. The only difference is the crate: shoe height here, far above the person's head there.
example_nl: De hond van de buren is klein.
alt: Een man staat naast een kist die niet hoger is dan zijn schoen.

scene: one plain wooden chair seen side-on on a flat floor line against a plain wall, standing half out of an opened cardboard packing box, the flaps folded down round its legs. The legs are straight and the seat and back smooth and unmarked. No bow. The wall is bare.
must: a smooth unmarked chair standing half out of its packing box.
avoid: a chair with cracks, a patched leg and a cobweb (oud-spullen); a chair with a bow tied on it (not the card); a chair on a shop shelf with a price tag (duur); a chair with a cushion (zacht).
contrast: Pair with oud-spullen. The only difference is the wear: smooth and still half in its packing box here, cracked and patched with a cobweb there.
alt: Een stoel met gladde poten staat half in een opengevouwen kartonnen doos.

scene: one plain wooden chair seen side-on on a flat floor line against a plain wall, with a long crack in the seat, a split back rail, one leg propped up with a folded wedge, and a cobweb in the corner of the back. The wall is bare.
must: a cracked, patched chair with a cobweb.
avoid: a smooth unmarked chair half out of its packing box (nieuw); a broken chair lying in pieces (kapot); a dirty chair with mud spots (vuil); an old person sitting on the chair (oud-mensen).
contrast: Pair with nieuw. The only difference is the wear: cracked and patched with a cobweb here, smooth and still half in its packing box there.
example_nl: Onze keukentafel is al heel oud.
example_en: Our kitchen table is already very old.
alt: Een stoel met een barst in de zitting, een steunblokje onder één poot en een spinnenweb.

scene: one plain wooden door in a plain wall, seen from the front, swung wide open towards the viewer so the empty doorway shows a plain room beyond, the hinges on the left, a round handle on the free edge. A flat floor line runs below and nobody is in view.
must: a door swung wide with the doorway empty.
avoid: a door shut in its frame (dicht); a door standing slightly ajar with a thin gap (open, not wide); a door with a person walking through (lopen); a door with a key in the lock (slot).
contrast: Pair with dicht. The only difference is the door leaf: swung wide with a gap to the room here, flush in the frame there.
example_nl: De winkel is op zondag open.
example_en: The shop is open on Sunday.
alt: Een deur is ver naar voren gedraaid; door het gat in de muur zie je een lege kamer.

scene: one plain wooden door in a plain wall, seen from the front, fitted flat and flush in its frame with no gap around it, the hinges on the left, a round handle on the right. A flat floor line runs below and nobody is in view.
must: a door flat in its frame with no gap.
avoid: a door swung wide with a room beyond (open); a door with a small gap showing light (open); a door with a large key (slot); a door with a person knocking (kloppen).
contrast: Pair with open. The only difference is the door leaf: flat in the frame with no gap here, swung wide there.
example_nl: Het raam in de keuken is dicht.
example_en: The window in the kitchen is closed.
alt: Een deur past precies in de muur en je ziet alleen de ronde deurknop.

scene: one adult stands whole-figure, front view, arms hanging, on a flat ground line with a plain wall behind, wearing a plain scarf hung round the neck whose two ends reach down to the knees. A small plain stool of fixed height stands on the ground beside the person.
must: a scarf hanging down to the knees.
avoid: a scarf ending at the chin (kort); a tall person (lang, the person sense: needs its own card); a thick scarf wrapped many times (dik); a scarf lying coiled on the ground (not the card).
contrast: Pair with kort. The only difference is the scarf ends: down at the knees here, level with the chin there.
example_nl: Mijn zus heeft heel lang haar.
example_en: My sister has very long hair.
alt: Een man heeft een sjaal om zijn nek; de uiteinden hangen tot zijn knieën.

scene: one adult stands whole-figure, front view, arms hanging, on a flat ground line with a plain wall behind, wearing a plain scarf round the neck whose two ends stop at the chin. A small plain stool of fixed height stands on the ground beside the person.
must: a scarf ending at the chin.
avoid: a scarf hanging down to the knees (lang); a small person next to the stool (klein); a thin scarf (dun); a scarf coiled on the ground (not the card).
contrast: Pair with lang. The only difference is the scarf ends: level with the chin here, down at the knees there.
example_nl: Mijn broer heeft altijd kort haar.
example_en: My brother always has short hair.
alt: Een man heeft een sjaal om zijn nek; de uiteinden eindigen bij zijn kin.

scene: one adult on a plain bicycle seen side-on, leaning forward, legs mid-turn, three bold speed lines trailing behind the bike and the wheels drawn slightly apart from the ground line. A small stone marker well behind the bike shows how far they have come from the start line.
must: a leaning cyclist with long speed lines behind the bike.
avoid: an upright rider with no lines (langzaam); a parked bike with a rider sitting still (not the card); dust clouds or smoke (not the style); a car or train (not the card).
contrast: Pair with langzaam. The only difference is the pace: speed lines and a leaning rider here, an upright rider with a snail at the wheel there.
alt: Een fietser leunt naar voren; achter de fiets lopen drie lange strepen.

scene: one adult on a plain bicycle seen side-on, sitting upright with both hands on the handlebar, feet barely turning the pedals, no speed lines. A small snail crawls on the ground right beside the front wheel, and a stone marker just behind the bike shows it has barely left the start line.
must: an upright cyclist with a snail beside the wheel.
avoid: a leaning cyclist with speed lines (snel); a parked bike with a rider sitting still (not the card); a sleeping snail with eyes shut (not the card); a person walking uphill (steil).
contrast: Pair with snel. The only difference is the pace: an upright rider with a snail at the wheel here, speed lines and a leaning rider there.
example_nl: De oude bus rijdt heel langzaam.
example_en: The old bus drives very slowly.
alt: Een fietser zit rechtop; naast het voorwiel kruipt een slak.

scene: one plain vase holding one flower with a straight stem and a round head of petals, not a tulip, stands centred on a plain table, front view. The vase is intact and smooth with an even, regular swirl pattern. One adult at the right, head and shoulders, looks at it with raised brows and a soft smile.
must: an even swirl on the vase and an admiring face beside it.
avoid: the same vase with clashing blotches and a grimacing onlooker (lelijk); a vase with a large bow (not the card); a tidy empty vase (leeg); a vase broken in pieces (kapot).
contrast: Pair with lelijk. The only difference is the pattern and the onlooker: an even swirl and an admiring face here, clashing blotches and a grimace there.
example_nl: Wat een mooie tuin heb jij!
example_en: What a beautiful garden you have!
alt: Een vaas met een regelmatig krulpatroon en één bloem; een man ernaast kijkt er glimlachend naar.

scene: one plain vase holding one flower with a straight stem and a round head of petals, not a tulip, stands centred on a plain table, front view. The vase is intact, the same shape, covered in clashing blotches and jagged stripes that collide. One adult at the right, head and shoulders, pulls the brows together, wrinkles the nose and twists the mouth sideways.
must: clashing blotches on the vase and a grimacing face beside it.
avoid: the same vase with an even swirl and an admiring onlooker (mooi); a vase broken in pieces (kapot); a vase with a wilted flower (dood); a dirty vase with mud spots (vuil); an onlooker with V-shaped brows and a tight mouth (boos).
contrast: Pair with mooi. The only difference is the pattern and the onlooker: clashing blotches and a grimace here, an even swirl and an admiring face there.
example_nl: Ik vind die jas echt lelijk.
example_en: I think that coat is really ugly.
alt: Een vaas vol botsende vlekken en strepen met één bloem; een man ernaast trekt een vies gezicht.

scene: one adult in plain clothes with a bag stands calmly at a plain bus stop beside a post with a blank sign plate, whole figure, side view. Far down the plain road at the left, one plain bus is still approaching, drawn small. The adult waits, relaxed, looking toward it. No sun, moon, clock or numerals.
must: the adult waiting while the bus is still far away and coming.
avoid: the bus driving off with the adult running after it (laat); a sun rising at the horizon (ochtend); a moon and stars (nacht); the adult stepping onto the bus (instappen); a clock face (not the card).
contrast: Pair with laat. The only difference is the bus and the adult: the bus still coming and the adult waiting here, the bus driving off and the adult running after it there.
alt: Een man met een tas wacht bij een bushalte; de bus is nog ver weg en komt eraan.

scene: the same adult in plain clothes with a bag at the plain bus stop beside a post with a blank sign plate, whole figure, side view. The plain bus is already pulling away at the right edge of the road, and the adult runs after it, one arm raised, mouth open, bag swinging. No sun, moon, clock or numerals.
must: the bus driving off while the adult runs after it.
avoid: the adult waiting while the bus is still coming (vroeg); a moon and stars over a house (nacht); a sun rising at the horizon (ochtend); a person running with speed lines and no bus (snel); a clock face (not the card).
contrast: Pair with vroeg. The only difference is the bus and the adult: the bus driving off and the adult running after it here, the bus still coming and the adult waiting there.
example_nl: Ik ben te laat voor de bus.
example_en: I am too late for the bus.
alt: Een man met een tas rent achter een bus aan die net wegrijdt van de halte.
